did.unittitle: Altmar, N.Y. Congregational Church of Sand Bank records, 1886-1913.
did.abstract: The First Congregational Church, also named the Congregational Church of Sand Bank, in Altmar, New York, was gathered in 1852 and was the successor church of the previously established First Presbyterian Church. Church buildings were completed in 1840 and 1876. The church was dissolved by 1914. This collection contains a single church record book and some correspondence with the American Congregational Union.

bioghist.head: Historical Note
bioghist.p: The First Presbyterian Church of Albian was gathered in the village of Sand Bank on January 27, 1829. Meetings were initially held in a school house. Construction on a church edifice began in 1834 and was completed in 1840. In 1852, the First Presbyterian Church was reorganized as the First Congregational Church with Rev. Thomas Salmon as the first installed minister. The name of the church is variously called the First Congregational Church and the Congregational Church of Sand Bank depending on the source. Construction on a new church building began in 1870 and the dedication for the building was held on June 2, 1876. A fire destroyed much of the village's center in 1885, though the church building largely escaped the worst of the damage. In 1886, the church underwent renovations. By 1914, the church was dissolved.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This collection contains a single church record book from the Congregational Church of Sand Bank, also known as the First Congregational Church, in Altmar, New York as well as some correspondence with the American Congregational Union. A copy of the church's covenant is pasted into the front of the record book.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Materials in this collection have been arranged into chronological order by start date.
